newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to sign intelligence reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to sign intelligence reform bill.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will sign a bill to modestly restructure U.S. intelligence operations, overriding objections from CIA Director John Deutch to a provision affecting his agency, the Washington Post reported on Saturday, quoting White House officials.

The bill would give the FBI an explicit right to subpoena local telephone records and would authorise the CIA and National Security Agency to collect data on foreign citizens for U.S. law enforcement agencies.

It would also require Senate confirmation of the CIA's general counsel, an action meant to preclude undue political influence over a post responsible for blocking illegal covert action, the newspaper reported.
But Deutch is opposing another provision of the bill which would create three new assistant director jobs, reporting to a new deputy director of central intelligence for community management.
Deutch has said he felt the new positions would not be useful and "will add an unnecessary level of political appointees."

In a letter to Sen. Arlen Specter, the Pennsylvania Republican who chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, on Sept. 20, Deutch said he planned to recommend that Clinton seek repeal of the new positions or substantial revision in the next Congress.
